profile.summary: GPN-Promoter (Hugging Face name gpn-animal-promoter) is a DNA language model trained on 512-bp promoter windows from 434 animal genomes. It was released with TraitGym, a benchmark of causal regulatory variants in human genetics. Given a DNA window, it predicts masked nucleotides; the GPN tools turn this into a variant score, the log-likelihood ratio of the alternate against the reference allele, or into sequence embeddings.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: GPN-Promoter belongs to the GPN (GPN-SS) family: single-sequence genomic language models trained on unaligned genomes with masked language modelling. The paper trains it on 512-bp windows centred on the transcription start sites of protein-coding genes, with base-pair tokens and repeat positions (soft-masked in the reference genome) down-weighted to 0.01. The architecture follows ByteNet: blocks that alternate dilated convolutions and feed-forward layers. The published config has 64 layers and hidden size 1024, a first kernel size of 9 and later kernel size of 5, with dilation base 2 cycling every 8 layers. The vocabulary has 7 tokens, from the tokenizer gonzalobenegas/tokenizer-dna-mlm named in the training script. Training ran 370K steps at batch size 2048, which took about 2 weeks on 4 NVIDIA A100 40GB GPUs. For variant scoring, the GPN package compares the model's likelihood of the alternate and reference alleles, averaged over both strands.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: One model is published, songlab/gpn-animal-promoter, read here at revision 7cf3276a. Intermediate training checkpoints from the same run are in a separate Hugging Face dataset, and the training data are in songlab/gpn-animal-promoter-dataset. The analysis code that produced the model is preserved under the ref analysis-archive-2026-08-18 of the GPN repository. The model card imports gpn.model, while the current GPN docs (commit dc5fd287 read here) load GPN models through register_auto_classes("ss"). A result should name the Hugging Face revision and the GPN package version used to load it.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Masked DNA language model (GPN single-sequence family) trained on animal promoter sequences, used for zero-shot variant effect prediction.
facts.source_locator: docs/models/gpn.md; Hugging Face API cardData tags

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: GPN model with a ByteNet-style dilated convolutional encoder: 64 layers, hidden size 1024, intermediate size 2048, embedding size 768, kernel size 9 then 5, dilation base 2 with cycle 8. The paper's Table S6 gives an embedding dimension of 1024 and 64 convolutional blocks; config.json gives hidden_size 1024 and a separate embedding_size of 768, and the files read do not say how the two relate.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: DNA sequence windows tokenised with a 7-token DNA tokenizer. The GPN variant-scoring command takes biallelic SNVs (chrom, one-based pos, ref, alt), a genome FASTA and a window size.

quotes.text: VEP inputs must be biallelic SNVs: `ref` and `alt` are distinct, uppercase, single characters from `A`, `C`, `G`, and `T`.

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Masked-nucleotide predictions or embeddings from the model; through the GPN tools, a raw, uncalibrated alternate-minus-reference log-likelihood ratio per variant (negative means the alternate is less likely), averaged over both strands. In TraitGym the authors also use the L2 distance between reference and alternate embeddings as a zero-shot score, chosen for complex traits.
facts.source_locator: model card; GPN CLI docs; paper: Table S9

quotes.text: In particular, negative values mean the alternate is less likely than the reference under the model.

facts.value: 152,189,952 in the published safetensors file, as counted by Hugging Face. The paper gives 152M.

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: 512-bp sequences centred on the transcription start sites of protein-coding genes, from 434 animal reference genomes. Species with gene annotations at NCBI Datasets were subsampled to at most one per family. Published as the Hugging Face dataset songlab/gpn-animal-promoter-dataset.

strengths.text: It needs only a single sequence, not a whole-genome alignment, unlike GPN-MSA and GPN-Star in the same repository.

limitations.text: It is trained only on 512-bp promoter windows. In TraitGym its zero-shot scores did better on proximal non-exonic and 5' UTR variants, the regions closest to its training data, than on other variant classes.

run_guide.summary: Install the GPN package and load the GPN-Promoter masked language model from Hugging Face.
prerequisites: Python 3.13, which the GPN package supports; its Transformers version is pinned.
For CUDA, install PyTorch with the official installer before or alongside GPN. Hardware needs are not stated.
Weights and code are MIT licensed; the weights are not gated.

steps.title: Install GPN
steps.explanation: Installs the model architectures, AutoClass registration, NumPy, PyTorch and Transformers.

quotes.text: This base installation contains the supported model architectures, explicit AutoClass registration, NumPy, PyTorch, Transformers, and jaxtyping.

steps.title: Load the model
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
from gpn import register_auto_classes
from transformers import AutoModelForMaskedLM

register_auto_classes("ss")

model = AutoModelForMaskedLM.from_pretrained("songlab/gpn-animal-promoter")
PY
steps.explanation: The GPN docs' quick-start snippet for the GPN family, wrapped in a shell heredoc, with the model name taken from the GPN-Promoter model card in place of songlab/gpn-brassicales. The model card's own snippet imports gpn.model instead.

notes: GPN-Promoter is the name used in TraitGym; the Hugging Face model is songlab/gpn-animal-promoter and the docs call it the animal promoter model. Revision of 2026-11-27: the TraitGym preprint (bioRxiv v2) is now read; it confirms the record's attributes (434 animal genomes, 512 bp around TSS, at most one species per family).
